classification.difficultyReason: Derive horizontal centre separation from radius sums and differences, recognise that two separations add to the third, and isolate the smallest radius in the resulting radical equation.

content.prompt: Three circles of radii $r_1<r_2<r_3$ are mutually tangent and also tangent to a horizontal line, as shown in the diagram below. Find an expression for $r_1$ in terms of $r_2$ and $r_3$.

spec.description: Largest circle left, middle circle right, smallest circle in the lower gap; all three touch the common baseline. Decorative fills omitted.
spec.mathematics: Mutual external tangency and baseline tangency; radius order r1<r2<r3. Coordinates are an illustrative configuration, not additional numerical givens.

answer.short:
$r_1=\dfrac{r_2r_3}{(\sqrt{r_2}+\sqrt{r_3})^2}$.

The two horizontal separations involving the smallest circle add to the separation of the larger circles.
answer.worked:
For two tangent circles of radii $u,v$ on the same horizontal line, their centre heights differ by $u-v$ and their centre distance is $u+v$. If their horizontal separation is $x$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=(u+v)^2-(u-v)^2\\x^2&=4uv\\x&=2\sqrt{uv}.\end{align*}$$
The smallest circle's centre lies horizontally between the other two centres, so
$$\begin{align*}2\sqrt{r_1r_3}+2\sqrt{r_1r_2}&=2\sqrt{r_2r_3}\\\sqrt{r_1}(\sqrt{r_3}+\sqrt{r_2})&=\sqrt{r_2r_3}\\\sqrt{r_1}&=\frac{\sqrt{r_2r_3}}{\sqrt{r_2}+\sqrt{r_3}}\\r_1&=\frac{r_2r_3}{(\sqrt{r_2}+\sqrt{r_3})^2}.\end{align*}$$
